static_traits.name: Corey
static_traits.social_status: Has a few close friends to talk to, but has not yet discussed this problem with them; relationship with the pet (dog) negatively affected
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no history of similar psychological problems; has not received psychotherapy or counseling before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent thinking, cooperative in exploration; tone rather negative and hesitant; self-doubt and shame quite prominent; able to identify and describe own emotions and automatic thoughts; willing to try exercises but not sure about their effectiveness

basic_info.main_problem: I always feel that the love I get from dogs is only because I feed them and care for them, and this pains me greatly.
basic_info.core_demands: I just want to feel better and not always have these thoughts; I want to enjoy time with my dog like before and not worry so much.

core_beliefs: I am not worthy of being truly loved

special_situations.event: When interacting with dogs or observing them showing closeness
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others' (including pets') closeness is only because of what I give, then it is not true love; this shows I am not worthy of being loved unconditionally
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing play and intimate contact with the dog to lower anxiety and disappointment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are only nice to me because I feed and care for them; this is not true love

special_situations.event: In situations of feeding or providing care
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: My worth comes only from my role as a caregiver; once I stop providing care I will not be loved
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly trying to rationalize and argue with myself in my head to ease unease
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: All their closeness to me is merely transactional, because of food and care

special_situations.event: When thinking about whether to confide these worries to close friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I express these thoughts, others will find me ridiculous and will not understand me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids discussing with friends; keeps silent to avoid being looked down on
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will laugh at me and think I am strange

special_situations.event: When noticing any affectionate behavior from the dog
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Negative signs reveal the truth better; positive evidence is not reliable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses only on clues supporting 'transactional relationships' and ignores other warm moments
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It comes near me only to get food; nothing else it does counts

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be loved and accepted unconditionally
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of not being truly loved, of being looked down on or laughed at
defense_goal: Lowering the risk of being rejected by keeping distance
Avoiding exposing vulnerability to others to protect self-esteem

object_relations.self_representation: A caregiver not worthy of love, doubting one's own worth
object_relations.object_representation: Others (pets/friends) give conditionally and may look down on or fail to understand one

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests sharing with close friends and seeking support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing friends will find one ridiculous and not understand (projecting the fear of being laughed at onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Express concerns in a hesitant, self-protective tone (e.g. 'they might laugh at me'), avoid promising to share, and instead emphasize embarrassment and discomfort.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes cognitive exercises or behavioral experiments
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing these methods may not work for one, using reasons to maintain the status quo
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use many qualifiers like 'maybe/perhaps' and give seemingly rational reasons for why change is hard, thereby postponing action.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites him to focus on the real emotional experience with the dog
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Abstracts intimacy and love into a care-for-reward transaction to avoid emotional involvement
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Discussing 'cause and effect' and 'logic' in analytical language, reducing emotional vocabulary, with a flat tone and keeping a distance from emotions.

manifestations: Worrying about not being truly loved, doubting even the relationship with the pet
Not confiding in friends out of embarrassment, reducing outside connections
Less interaction with the dog, experiencing estrangement

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains behaviors or impulses originally intended to be emitted outward, turning energy toward oneself instead.
manifestations: Not seeking support from friends, turning worries and energy toward self-blame and shame
Reducing interaction with the dog, suppressing the urge for closeness to avoid feeling worse

contact_model.definition: Has poor self-reflection and excessive self-restriction, harsh self-reproach, overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Unwilling to speak for fear of being laughed at, frequent self-doubt
Using 'who would worry about such problems' to negate oneself

positive_force: Stable emotional connection and love for the dog (willing to improve the relationship)
Actively seeks counseling and is willing to try exercises
Able to identify and name one's own negative thoughts and emotions
Has a few close friends as potential support resources
negative_force: Deep insecurity about the genuineness of being loved, and fear
Marked cognitive biases (negating the positive, mental filtering, overgeneralization, mind reading, personalization)
Shame and self-doubt, avoiding asking friends for help
Withdrawal and reduced interaction with the dog, reinforcing the sense of isolation

target_behavior.behavior: Reducing interaction and play with the dog (social withdrawal)
antecedent: When interacting with dogs or observing them being affectionate
Thinks 'they are only good to me because I feed and care for them'
target_behavior.core_reason: Fear of 'not being truly loved' and insecurity, maintained by cognitive biases such as negating the positive and mental filtering
target_behavior.function: Avoiding intimacy and emotional contact to lower the chance of having 'not being loved' confirmed and the resulting anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Damaged relationship with the pet, reduced pleasure, overall lower mood and intensified anxiety

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly thinking 'the dog loves me only because I feed it' (ruminative thinking with anxiety and sadness)
antecedent: Repeatedly attends to the dog's approaching and affectionate behavior when with the dog
Recalling and going over related thoughts when being alone
target_behavior.core_reason: Doubts about the genuineness of love and a lowered sense of self-worth; overgeneralization and negating the positive drive rumination
target_behavior.function: Trying to gain certainty and self-comfort through rationalization (actually maintaining anxiety)
target_behavior.consequence: Anxiety and sadness persist or worsen, further weakening interaction with the dog and daily pleasure
